module_title: CKA Week 3 - Cluster Maintenance, etcd, Logging and Monitoring
title: CKA Week 3 Challenge - Maintenance, etcd, Logging
description: End-of-week challenge for maintenance and observability: drain a node safely, take and verify an etcd snapshot exactly like the exam, restore with etcdutl, and drill the logging commands.
scenario: Week 3 in one lab: the tasks you cannot afford to hesitate on. The etcd backup flow here is the exam flow - a control-plane pod with hostPath mounts of the etcd certs, snapshot to local disk, verify, restore into a fresh data-dir. (kubeadm upgrade itself needs real VMs - practice that on the Tuesday/Wednesday VM drills from your plan.)
symptoms: bare-worker is a pod with no controller: draining evicts it permanently - the perfect drain proof
fail-log crash-loops on purpose so logs --previous always has material
The k3s static manifests are mounted read-only at /k3s-manifests for inspection
mission: Prove a safe drain, take a verified etcd snapshot and restore from it, and capture the observability evidence (logs --previous, top, events, describe) the exam asks for.

hints.title: Drain proof
hints.content: bare-worker has no owner References, so after drain + uncordon it is gone for good - that is your proof the drain actually evicted it. Deployments come back; bare pods do not.

hints.title: The exam etcd flow
hints.content: On the exam you run etcdctl ON the control plane with the certs from /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd. Here the helper pod mounts the k3s equivalents (/tls) and talks to 127.0.0.1:2379 via hostNetwork - same steps, same flags, copy them exactly.

hints.title: snapshot status is offline
hints.content: etcdctl snapshot status works on the file alone - no cluster contact. Use it to verify /root/etcd-backup.db is a real snapshot.

hints.title: Restore does not touch the running cluster
hints.content: etcdutl snapshot restore --data-dir only builds a NEW data directory from the snapshot. Pointing the server at it (manifest --data-dir edit) is the exam step you practice on real VMs.

acceptance_criteria.description: Drain (--ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data) then uncordon: bare-worker evicted, node schedulable
etcd-helper pod Running in kube-system (k3s image, hostNetwork, /tls + /snapshots hostPaths)
etcd snapshot saved via helper and copied to /root/etcd-backup.db (valid snapshot file)
/root/snapshot-status.txt captures the snapshot status table (DB size present)
Restore drilled: etcdutl restore produced /snapshots/restored/member inside the helper
/root/crash.log captures logs --previous of the crash-looping fail-log deployment
/root/top-pods.txt has live metrics-server output for all pods
/root/static-manifests.txt lists the k3s static pod manifests (coredns visible)
/root/node-describe.txt is a node describe output containing Conditions
etcd endpoint health verified through the helper
